title.narrative: Improving judicial administration in HJCP, SNCA
Improving judicial administration in HJCP, SNCA

description.narrative: The ICEA 3 programme has requested the Embassy of Sweden to support 9 components (projects). HJPC will be asked to remove components 7 and 9 of the programme in whole or in part before final decision on the programme. These components are highlighted in appraisal. 1. Enhanced conditions for a more efficient use of the court staffs particular knowledge and skills especially of non-judicial staff 2. Improved system for redistribution of cases among available judges in the court and more adequate application of the Book of Rules on Indicative Performance Measures for Judges and Legal Associates in Courts in BiH 3. Enhanced conditions for a reform on a more efficient appeal procedure for civil litigation in BiH 4. Enhanced conditions for a more efficient enforcement procedure in pilot courts in BiH. 5. Improved conditions for judicial institutions to plan and start implementing the Strategy for Improving Gender Equality in the Judiciary in BiH. 6. Improve the position of vulnerable groups in contact with the justice system 7. Improving energy efficiency, security and removing barriers for people with disabilities 8. Enhanced conditions for a continuous proactive and effective communication with the citizens via media 9. Module for Electronic Evidence Management (MEME) established in the BiH judiciary

Projektet är en fortsättning på stöd för förbättrad effektivitet inom HJPC. Resultaten av den tredje fasen är att förbättra domstolarnas effektivitet och även verkställigheten av domstolsärenden. Effekten av stödet är att ha ett domstolssystem som garanterar människor rätten till en rättvis rättegång inom rimlig tid.
Detta är en förutsättning för anslutning till EU-medlemskap. Effekterna av projektet kommer också att bidra till att förbättra allmänhetens uppfattning om domstolssystem och också leda till en mer funktionell ekonomi.

The project is a continuation of support to improved efficiency within HJPC. The results of the third phase are to improve the efficiency of courts and also enforcement of court cases. The effect of the support is to have a court system that guarantees people the right to a fair trial within a reasonable time.
This is a prerequisite for accession to EU membership. The effects of the project will also contribute to improving the public's perception of court systems and also lead to a more functional economy.

Component 1: Legislation Development, Strategic Planning and Policy Advocacy (Covers former Components 2, 3, 4, 5a, 5b, 6 where relevant to HJPC policy, standards, and systemlevel reforms) Significant progress has been made in strengthening HJPCs capacity to lead legislative and policy reforms. The system for monitoring human resources across 16 courts is now operational, enabling more transparent and equitable workload distribution and informing future amendments to the Book of Rules on Performance Targets. Analytical groundwork for civil appeal reform has been completed, including a situation analysis, comparative EU study, and the final reform proposal, all of which have been disseminated to key stakeholders. In the area of enforcement, the project produced concrete proposals for reorganising enforcement work, including new working methods and competence requirements for bailiffs. A Blueprint with recommendations has been finalised and shared, and structured dialogue with pilot courts confirms uptake and readiness for further policy development. So far, only the Municipal Court Sarajevo has actually operationalised it in practice.The enforcement component in ICEA is expected to support onboarding of new courts during the next phase. Genderequality reforms have advanced at the strategic level. Judicial institutions action plans have been assessed and approved, and the HJPCs role as a focal point for gender equality has been strengthened through guidelines on preventing sexual and genderbased harassment, gender analysis of court decisions, and expanded cooperation with NGOs and international partners.
Work on vulnerable groups has contributed to policylevel awareness through targeted analyses, including the recent assessment of discrimination cases, which provides an evidence base for future reforms. Overall, HJPCs legislative, policy and strategicplanning functions have been reinforced, improving the likelihood of achieving the objectives under this component. Component 2: Support to Further Reorganisation of Business Models in Judicial Institutions and Rollout (Covers former Components 1, 2, 4, 5a, 6) The project has delivered strong results in improving business processes and organisational models in firstinstance courts. The revised Blueprint and annexes now provide a comprehensive operational framework, and new job descriptions for trainees, judicial assistants and additional staff categories have laid the foundation for more efficient utilisation of nonjudicial personnel. Peerlearning with Swedish sister courts has supported practical uptake of new work methods, and capacitybuilding for trainees, assistants and mentor judges has strengthened implementation capacity. Pilot courts have demonstrated measurable improvements in efficiency. The introduction of equal starting parameters and the new casedistribution model has contributed to higher implementation rates of backlogreduction plans and reduced average case duration. In enforcement, several courtsmost notably Sarajevohave achieved substantial improvements, with enforcement rates rising from 5% in 2022 to 45% in 2024, demonstrating the potential for replication. Genderequality implementation at the institutional level has progressed, with judicial institutions beginning to operationalise their action plans and integrate gender considerations into daily work. Training activities and pilot approaches have supported this transition. Work on accessibility and treatment of vulnerable groups has improved courts ability to respond to user needs, supported by staff training, architectural assessments and targeted publications such as My Guide to Criminal Process. Overall, the foundations for more efficient, systematic and sustainable work processes are in place, and the rollout potential is strong. Component 3: Proactive Transparency, Communications and Outreach (Covers former Components 6 and 7) The project has strengthened the judiciarys communication practices and transparency mechanisms. A media communication toolkit and a Media Action Plan have been developed, and implementation has begun across pilot courts.
Peer learning and support for transparency initiatives such as open court days and regular press briefings, have increased courts engagement with the public. Additional data collection during the extension period has provided insights into webportal usage and the quality and quantity of published information, informing a final report with recommendations for further improvement. A new advisory body is planned at Council level, which will support institutionalisation of communication practices. Awareness of the rights of vulnerable groups has increased through targeted analyses and improved cooperation with NGOs, contributing to more inclusive communication and outreach
